title: Pause + Return
concept: Designed to turn “I need space” into a promise rather than a slammed door: time apart, with a set time to come back. Asking for a pause never counts against you. It’s one of the tools we reach for most.
whenToUse: When either of you is flooded: your heart is racing, you’ve got tunnel vision, you can’t think straight, and you want to flee or to win. By then it isn’t calm enough for an honest conversation.
steps: Say it — “I need a pause.” You don’t have to explain.
Set a time — pick when you’ll be back, at least 20 minutes and at most 24 hours away: “I’ll be ready at ___.”
Step away — get calm (walk, shower, breathe, music). Don’t rehearse the argument in your head.
Come back — reconnect at the time you said, even briefly, to prove it’s a pause, not a disappearance.
Restart warm — warm up and check it’s safe before you go back to “where you left off.”

phrases.text: I’m not leaving you; I just need to get calm.

working: B: “I’m flooded. I need a pause. I’ll be ready at 9.15pm.” A: “Okay. Thank you for giving a time. I’ll see you at 9.15pm.” They return at 9.15pm, even for two minutes, then restart warm.
notWorking: B says, “I need space. We’ll talk later,” and walks away. “Later” isn’t a return time. A is left in the kitchen, watching the clock for a time that was never set.
activity: Agree your default length (say, 20 minutes) and your max (24 hours). Agree your phrases out loud and write them down. Practise once this week on something minor, and keep the return time.
warn: For flooding, never for fear. If threats, fear, coercion or violence appear, do not return at the set time: leave safely and use the Help Lines.
